_meta.note: Real receipt library owned and signed off by the receipts workstream. Each receipt is a fact, stat, story, or opinion Rahul can honestly claim. Never Rahul's own brand/company name in ids or text (see HARD RULES / MASTER_PROMPT); third-party tools (Lovable, VdoCipher) are fine. ids are passed verbatim to the drafting model, so keep ids free of Rahul's own brand too. Topics feed both rank_receipts and the triage vocabulary; keep clusters distinct so no two receipts always co-surface on the same tweet.
_meta.confirm_before_ship_note: The ONLY ground-truth facts are the original 7: 70k+ paid learners, price-signal-trust, 4%/38% micropaywall show-up, Lovable 6wk build + DRM, in-person writing programs in Dehradun/Bangalore, Meta/Google perf marketing on Indian budgets, 36 months bootstrapped. Every receipt id listed below asserts a first-person NUMBER, OUTCOME, or lived STORY that is NOT covered by those 7, yet is stated as fact and injected verbatim to the drafting model — so it can surface in a live reply as Rahul's own claim. Because fabricated stats/outcomes are banned by the HARD RULES, Rahul must confirm each of these is literally true before go-live. Until confirmed, treat them as unverified.
confirm_before_ship: referral-quietly-cheapest: asserts word-of-mouth from past learners is the cheapest, highest-trust channel and closes 'without spending a rupee' (channel-economics claim; formerly the ~3% referral-share number, now qualitative but still an unverified outcome).
waitlist-warms-the-room: asserts the fastest-filling cohorts were preceded by weeks of talking to a warm waitlist (formerly the 40%-roster number; the causal outcome remains unverified).
discount-attracts-worst-buyers: asserts refund and support load rose every time a heavy discount ran (a lived operational outcome, not in the 7 facts).
profit-buys-patience: asserts the company was profitable and could 'wait out a bad quarter' — goes beyond the confirmed 'bootstrapped 36 months' into a specific profitability + runway claim.
first-hire-was-a-doer: a specific hiring story (who the first real hire was and the counterfactual 'I'd have grown faster') not in the 7 facts.

hook-carries-the-ad: asserts the first three seconds 'decide almost everything' on Rahul's ad account, and that a sharp hook beats a better offer 'every time' — a stronger causal claim than the confirmed perf-marketing fact.

drm-piracy-tradeoff: asserts a specific empirical piracy-behavior OUTCOME (DRM 'stopped the casual re-uploads but never the determined pirates'). The 7 facts only confirm DRM was *added* (Lovable 6wk build + DRM), not this observed outcome. Text softened to a non-empirical intent framing, but confirm the outcome claim before restoring or citing the harder version.

cohort-shows-up-for-people: a lived cohort-behavior claim ('someone in the group would notice if they didn't show up') presented as observed fact; borderline general observation but confirm it reflects real cohort behavior before go-live.

content-was-never-the-moat: the 70,000 figure was removed here so only 70k-learners carries it, but the remaining opinion still asserts the accountability-is-the-moat outcome drawn from Rahul's own cohorts; confirm it reflects his real view.

3% referral share, ~11pt trial lift, 40% waitlist roster, 3-line lesson rule: original illustrative numbers were scrubbed from the shipped text; if Rahul wants any of them restored, confirm the literal figure first.

receipts.text: Indian buyers price-signal trust, not affordability. Drop a price to look accessible and you read as low-stakes; the ones who convert want to feel they bought something serious.
receipts.use_when: positioning, premium vs cheap, how a price reads, trust signals

receipts.text: Free webinars got me about 4% show-up. A small paid deposit took it to roughly 38%. The money wasn't the filter, the commitment was.
receipts.use_when: funnels, free vs paid, no-shows, lead quality, deposits

receipts.text: Every time I ran a heavy discount, the refund and support load went up, not down. Cheapest buyers ask the most and trust the least.
receipts.use_when: discounts, sales, 'just lower the price' takes, refund pain

receipts.text: Built our masterclass app on Lovable in 6 weeks, DRM and all, before I'd have finished scoping it the old way. The bottleneck was never the code.
receipts.use_when: building with AI, shipping speed, no-code, solo founder velocity

receipts.text: We added DRM to our course video knowing a determined pirate gets through anything. I treat it as a signal to honest buyers, not a wall. The point was never to be uncrackable.
receipts.use_when: piracy, content protection, DRM, over-engineering security

receipts.text: We're past 70,000 paid learners now. The thing that scaled wasn't content, it was the reason people trusted us with their money.
receipts.use_when: scale, audience, edtech, trust at volume

receipts.text: Everyone thinks the course is the product. After enough cohorts I'm sure the product is the accountability around it. Content is the cheapest part to copy, so it was never the moat.
receipts.use_when: moats, defensibility, what people actually pay for, why content is commoditized

receipts.text: I run in-person writing programs in Dehradun and Bangalore. Thousands of photos in, the single biggest retention lever is people meeting in a room, not the curriculum.
receipts.use_when: community, in-person, cohorts, retention, writing

receipts.text: People don't finish a course for the certificate. They finish it because someone in the group would notice if they didn't show up.
receipts.use_when: completion rates, motivation, community, accountability

receipts.text: Running Meta and Google on small-to-mid Indian budgets teaches you fast that creative fatigue kills you before CPMs do. I refresh angles before the numbers even dip.
receipts.use_when: paid ads, performance marketing, creative, CAC

receipts.text: On our ad account the first three seconds decide almost everything. I've watched a mediocre offer with a sharp hook beat a great offer with a soft one, every time.
receipts.use_when: ad creative, hooks, thumbnails, first-line-matters takes

receipts.text: Our cheapest, highest-trust channel was never an ad. Word of mouth from past learners closes without me spending a rupee, it just doesn't show up in a dashboard.
receipts.use_when: CAC, channels, organic vs paid, word of mouth, attribution

receipts.text: A waitlist isn't a vanity list, it's a warm-up. The cohorts that filled fastest were the ones where I'd been talking to the room for weeks before opening.
receipts.use_when: launches, waitlists, demand, pre-selling, audience building

receipts.text: 36 months bootstrapped in India. The freedom people romanticize is real but it's paid for in the deals you say no to when raising would've made them easy.
receipts.use_when: bootstrapping vs raising, founder tradeoffs, discipline

receipts.text: Being profitable didn't make us fast, it made us patient. We could wait out a bad quarter instead of pitching through it. That patience is the whole advantage.
receipts.use_when: profitability, runway, raising, slow vs fast growth

receipts.text: I'd rather be read as an operator than a guru. People trust the person still doing the boring work over the one who's graduated to selling the framework for it.
receipts.use_when: personal brand positioning, operator vs thought-leader, credibility, who to trust

receipts.text: The posts that landed for me were never the clever ones. They were the specific ones: one number, one moment, one thing I got wrong. Specific is what people trust.
receipts.use_when: writing advice, going viral, why content flops, specificity

receipts.text: My first real hire wasn't a strategist, it was someone who'd actually ship the boring work daily. I'd have grown faster if I'd stopped hiring people who thought like me.
receipts.use_when: hiring, first hires, team building, delegation

receipts.text: Every process we have exists because something broke first. I stopped trying to write the playbook in advance, the pain tells you exactly which one you actually need.
receipts.use_when: ops, systems, process, scaling a team, premature structure

receipts.text: When I try to teach ten things, people finish none. When I teach one thing they can use tomorrow, they come back for the next. Scope is the lesson.
receipts.use_when: teaching, curriculum, course design, scope, learning
